fw_at_the_ramp_foot.description:
Warden Hesk Stonefoot watches everything that comes up the ramp, because everything that reaches this city comes up it. He isn't a nervous man, and he's been nervous for a month.

Galak outriders have started standing at the bottom. They aren't blocking it. They're standing at it, in daylight, in numbers, where the whole Landing can look down and count them.
fw_at_the_ramp_foot.accept_text:
The Galak Khan's Chosen are the ones with the standard. Where they stand, the rest form up, and they've been forming up closer each week.

Go down and make the ground in front of that ramp expensive. I'm not asking for a war. I'm asking them to do their standing somewhere I can't see it from my own gate. Their Galak Wranglers hold the kodo back at Broadback, south-west of the ramp, so go that far.
fw_at_the_ramp_foot.turn_in_text:
They've moved back half a mile, in good order, which I notice.

Nobody routed them, they chose to go. That's worse, and I'm going to tell the council so whether they want to hear it or not.

fw_clay_up_the_ramp.description:
Potter Hesha will tell you that if you want to understand this city, you should stand at the bottom of the ramp for a day. Her clay comes up it in sacks from a pit four days west, and every pot in Freewind is priced to match.

There's clay in the salt pans south of the ramp, two days closer. Everyone's told her it won't fire, and nobody's tried it.
fw_clay_up_the_ramp.accept_text:
Dig me good sacks off the pans at Saltwatch, south of the ramp foot. Dig below the crust, because the crust is salt, and salt ruins a pot. Under it there's grey clay, and I want to see it.

The things that live out on those pans are made of the same salt. Don't let them get close enough to put it on you.
fw_clay_up_the_ramp.turn_in_text:
It really fires! It's pale, and it rings higher than the western clay, and it'll crack in the cold if the cold ever comes.

Two days closer makes it a different city.

fw_feed_below.description:
Stablemaster Reth keeps every four-legged animal in the city on the Landing, because kodo won't cross a rope bridge, and they worked that out faster than the tauren did.

That means the pens are up here and the feed is down there, and twice a season somebody has to go down and cut it. It's nobody's favourite week.
fw_feed_below.accept_text:
There's grass worth cutting in the wash beds. It's the only green on the whole floor, and it's green because that's where the year's water went.

Take a blade down and bring back what you can carry. Watch for scorpids in the shade of the cut banks. They're in there because it's cool, and they won't move for you. The best of the wash beds are under the Seam, north-west of the ramp foot, where the elk graze them down.
fw_feed_below.turn_in_text:
It smells like the plain. It doesn't taste like the plain, and the kodo know it, but they'll eat it.

Everything up here is a version of something we used to have.

fw_harpies_weave.description:
Bowyer Tesh builds better bows than her mother did, and she's never stopped being annoyed about why.

She's spent a season looking at harpy nests through a glass from the Windward top. They're woven, laid in courses like thatch, with a turn at the end of each course that she can't do and can't stop thinking about.
fw_harpies_weave.accept_text:
Bring me the weave. I don't want a handful of feathers. I want a piece with the courses still in it, big enough that I can see where the turn goes.

And yes, you'll have to kill the Sheerwing Harpies to get it. No, I haven't found a way round that, and I've thought about it more than you have.
fw_harpies_weave.turn_in_text:
Look at this. That's a bowyer's knot, or near enough, and it's being tied by something everyone in this city calls an animal.

I won't say that out loud yet. I'd like to be sure first, which is more courtesy than most of them get.

fw_hollowhorn_wants_less.description:
Quartermaster Bren Hollowhorn prices everything by the back that carried it up the ramp, and lately every back is costing more because of what's standing at the bottom.

She isn't interested in the philosophy. She has a column for what the escort costs, and she'd like it to be a smaller number by the end of the season.
fw_hollowhorn_wants_less.accept_text:
The wind-readers are what make a toll party work. They sit high and see a caravan's dust an hour out, and the riders are formed up and waiting before the drivers know they've been seen.

Take the readers out and the riders are guessing, and take enough of them and my escort column halves. The wind-readers are the Galak Windcatchers, and the ones under the standard are the Khan's Chosen, so kill both.
fw_hollowhorn_wants_less.turn_in_text:
It's down a third already, and I'll take a third.

You'll hear Namka say we should be talking to them. She's probably right, but she isn't the one buying rope.

fw_light_caravans.description:
Caravan-Master Bohl has been complaining about the ramp for three years, because the ramp is safe to complain about.

The real problem is on his tally sheet. Several caravans a week come up, and every one of them arrives lighter than it left, by an amount too regular to be theft and too large to be spillage. Somebody's taking a cut in the open, and the drivers have stopped mentioning it.
fw_light_caravans.accept_text:
The road east runs between the Sisters, and there's a gap you have to go through. That's where it happens.

Go and stand in that gap and see what it costs. They're Galak Outriders, and you'll have to kill them to get their tally slips. Bring me the slips. They write it down, and that's the part I can't get past. They aren't robbing us so much as invoicing us.
fw_light_caravans.turn_in_text:
It's itemised and dated, in a hand better than my clerk's.

I wanted to be angry about this, and now I've got to go and think about something else instead.

fw_older_than_the_wrong.description:
Spirit-Walker Enu has spent three years looking for the dead of Thunder Bluff and not finding them, and he's found the only comfort to be had in not finding them.

He's been out to Dryhollow twice. He wants somebody to carry this back and repeat it: what's wrong with Dryhollow was wrong before the Integration, and it'll be wrong after. Not everything broken in this world was broken by Earth arriving.
fw_older_than_the_wrong.accept_text:
Go out to Dryhollow, south of the ramp beyond the salt pans, and stand in the middle of it for as long as you can manage. Then come back and tell me what you felt.

The Dryhollow Basilisks won't let you stand anywhere for long, so thin them first. They're the oldest thing on this map, and they were doing this when the needles were still being cut by water.
fw_older_than_the_wrong.turn_in_text:
You felt nothing? Then that's the answer.

Everywhere the Integration touched feels like a held breath. Dryhollow feels like a room nobody's been in. It's simply old, and I needed one thing in this country to be simply old.

fw_one_road_in.description:
Sentry Palla says the single ramp is a better defence than Thunder Bluff ever had. She means it, and she knows exactly what it means to say it.

For the last two weeks, something has been working the bottom of the ramp after dark. It isn't attacking. It's testing, coming up far enough to be seen and then going back down, every night, a little further each time.
fw_one_road_in.accept_text:
I'm nearly sure it's hyena, and nearly sure is why I'm sending somebody instead of going myself.

Work the bottom of the ramp and the scrub on either side of it, kill the Dustmane Hyenas, and go out as far as the first bend of the Windward Road. If something's teaching them that this ramp is worth walking up, I want to know whether it's a pack or a person.
fw_one_road_in.turn_in_text:
It was only a pack, then.

I'd rather it were hunger than somebody's idea. I can post a sentry against hunger.

fw_pale_wood_wrong_wood.description:
Timberwright Gohn has stopped finding it strange that every plank in this city came off a mountain that wasn't here three years ago, and he's been told that's the strange part.

The bridges need relaying before the windy season, three spans. The rope gets all the attention, because rope is frightening and decking isn't, which is exactly backwards.
fw_pale_wood_wrong_wood.accept_text:
Mill me lengths at the bench, and bring up some sound bolts from the stacks to replace what you use.

Aspen takes a bend and holds it, which is why the bowyer's been insufferable lately, and it's why a deck board on a rope span wants to be aspen. Nothing that grew down here bends. The flood brings aspen down every year, and the Drowning Floor keeps it. The cave mouth is at the foot of Broadback, west of the ramp, and the blind kodo bed down on the stacks.
fw_pale_wood_wrong_wood.turn_in_text:
That's good work, and dull work, and dull work is what a bridge is made of.

When somebody walks across that span and thinks about the rope, they're thinking about the wrong thing, and that's the compliment.

fw_the_anvil.description:
Lookout Sima has the highest standing ground in Thousand Needles, and a list of the four mesas nobody has ever been on top of. The Anvil is the nearest of them.

For eleven nights there's been a light up there, and it isn't a fire, because a fire sits still. This moves along the rim and goes out and comes back, and she's counted the pattern, and it doesn't repeat.
fw_the_anvil.accept_text:
Get round the base of it and as high as the scree will take you. I'm not asking you to climb the unclimbable. I'm asking you to get close enough to see what's making that light.

The Sheerwing Rooktenders come down to hunt at dusk. Take a few on the way, and it'll be a quieter approach. The Anvil is the great flat rock at the far west end of the floor, past Needle's Eye, which is where you'll start meeting rooktenders.
fw_the_anvil.turn_in_text:
So something's carrying the light along the rim and putting it down.

Then they're signalling. Then that's something they do, and I've been writing them up as weather for three years.

fw_the_drowned.description:
The Rememberer holds the names of everyone who was in Thunder Bluff when the ground took the city, in order, and he says them through once a season. It takes most of a night, and he isn't going to stop.

Dral has told him what's down the hole at Broadback. There are things walking in it with salt set hard over them, and they have hands, and somebody somewhere has a list with their names on it.
fw_the_drowned.accept_text:
I'm not asking you to put them down out of mercy. You can decide that for yourself, and I wouldn't argue with either answer.

I'm asking you to bring back anything they carry that was made rather than grown, a notched stick, a ring, a tally, something that says a person kept it. Then I can say what they were before the water. They're in the Drowning Floor, the cave at the foot of Broadback, west of the ramp, and the crews call them saltbound shamblers.
fw_the_drowned.turn_in_text:
These are tally sticks, so they were salt crews, the ones who work the pans to the east and come back through the washes in the wet month.

Those are names I can find, and finding names is the only work I've ever been good at.

fw_the_glass_pan.description:
Relic-Keeper Dun can tell you whether a thing came up out of the mesas or down off the mountain. He can't always tell you what either one is, and he's honest about that, which is rarer in his trade than it should be.

A salt crew came back from the far side of Dryhollow talking about a pan fused to glass, a flat sheet of it with the sky in it. They wouldn't go nearer, and they wouldn't go back.
fw_the_glass_pan.accept_text:
Go and look at it, and bring me pieces off the edge.

The crew told me something lives out there and is still making the glass. Look at the pan, take your pieces off its rim, and don't go to the middle to find out what's standing there. Nothing I want is worth that. The glass pan is at the south edge of Dryhollow, south of the ramp and on past Saltwatch.
fw_the_glass_pan.turn_in_text:
It's fused all the way through, not glazed, as if it went through a kiln the size of the hollow.

I'll put this on the shelf and label it honestly: came up out of the mesas, cause unknown, don't go to the middle.

fw_the_parley.description:
High Elder Namka Windhollow built this city and can't get used to having built something again. She's listened to the warden, the quartermaster and the clerk, she's read the fourth column in the Galak ledger, and she's reached a conclusion the council will hate.

The Galak aren't raiding Freewind. They're charging it for a road they maintain, and nobody on either side has ever once said so out loud.
fw_the_parley.accept_text:
This goes to the Sisters, to whoever's standing in that gap, and it goes into a hand. Don't stick it in the ground or leave it on a stone.

They won't kill you for carrying it. They've never killed a driver who paid, and they've never killed one who couldn't. Walk up with it held where they can see it, and don't draw anything. If that frightens you, then you've understood the task.
fw_the_parley.turn_in_text:
They took it, and read it in front of you, and kept it?

Then we're talking. Three years, a dead road and a city in the air, and all it needed was somebody willing to walk up holding a piece of paper. I'll be a long time forgiving myself for those three years.

fw_the_road_is_open.description:
Namka has something she hasn't had in three years: a road, and somebody to talk to at both ends of it.

The Galak will let a caravan through, and the price is written down. The thing at the bottom of the hole under Broadback is dead. There's nothing left between Camp Taurajo and this city except distance, and the tauren have solved distance before.
fw_the_road_is_open.accept_text:
Take this north, all of it: the terms, the toll, the schedule, and the Galak's own hand at the bottom, which took longer to get than the rest put together.

Tull asked whether kodo could go down. Tell him yes. Tell him what it costs and who it costs, and tell him we're paying it and think the price is fair, and watch his face while you say that last part.
fw_the_road_is_open.turn_in_text:
It's signed by a centaur. There's a centaur's mark on a tauren document, and somebody expects me to read it out at the corral gate.

I drove that road for twenty years and never once paid a toll on it. I also never once had to ask who kept it up. All right, then, we'll pay.

fw_the_spill.description:
Skywatcher Rell can see the dark line of the aspen along the north on a clear day, and three years ago that line was sky.

Things have been coming down it, mostly elk. They came off the mountain into what looked like open country, walked south until the timber ran out, and found red hardpan and forty degrees of heat. They can't find the pass again. They stand on the Seam in the heat of the day, waiting for weather that isn't coming.
fw_the_spill.accept_text:
I'm not asking you to cull them, and I wouldn't call it that.

They're going down on their feet out there, and the cats came after them and are doing no better. Kill the Sunstruck Elk and the Downslope Lynx, and finish what the sun has started. Get close enough that it's quick. That's the whole task, and I'm sorry it's one.
fw_the_spill.turn_in_text:
You'll have seen the ribs on them.

We came down a pass too. The difference is that we knew what we were walking into, and we still argue about whether that was better.

fw_toll_ledger.description:
Tally-Clerk Nessa writes down everything that crosses this top. She'll tell you it isn't suspicion. It's that the tauren lost a city once without a list of what was in it.

Bohl has brought her a handful of Galak tally slips, and she hasn't slept properly since. They're better kept than hers, dated and carried forward, with a running balance and a column she can't identify.
fw_toll_ledger.accept_text:
I need more of it. I don't need slips. I need leaves out of the book the slips come from, and you'll find those on whoever is senior in a toll party.

I want to know what that fourth column is. If they're keeping a balance against us, then they think we owe them something specific, and I'd like to know what before the council decides for me.
fw_toll_ledger.turn_in_text:
It's a running total, against the road. They're charging us for the road itself, and they've been maintaining it.

There's a column for the upkeep too.

fw_where_the_water_goes.description:
Warehouse-Keeper Dral knows where everything that came up the ramp this season is, and he'll tell you to stop asking about anything that didn't.

What he can't account for is water. Thousand Needles floods once a year, hard, and then it's dry for twelve months. That much water doesn't evaporate. It goes somewhere, and whatever it goes into has been filling and emptying since before anyone here was born.
fw_where_the_water_goes.accept_text:
At the foot of Broadback, there's a wash that runs in and doesn't run out. Go and stand at the mouth of it and look down.

The Saltpan Kodo shelter in its mouth in the heat, and they won't like you there. Clear enough of them that you can get a proper look, and then come back and tell me how far down you could see before it stopped being down.
fw_where_the_water_goes.turn_in_text:
There was no bottom to it that you could see? A year's water, every year, into a hole with no bottom.

I've got a column in my book for things that go out and don't come back, and I'm going to need a bigger column.

fw_wrong_climate.description:
Healer Ilna Softstep treats falls, mostly, and off ladders rather than off edges. Lately she's been treating something else: drivers coming up the ramp with heat sickness in a season they've worked their whole lives.

She thinks the floor is getting hotter. She'd like to be wrong, and she's worked out a way to find out that doesn't depend on her being right.
fw_wrong_climate.accept_text:
Bring me marrow from the elk dying on the Seam, and a scrape of the ground they're dying on.

An animal that starves and an animal that cooks don't leave the same marrow. If it's the heat, I'll know, and I'll have to go and tell Namka that the floor is changing under a city that can't move.
fw_wrong_climate.turn_in_text:
It's the heat, not hunger.

I wanted it to be hunger. Hunger would have meant they were simply in the wrong place, and this means the place is going wrong.

fw_yearmaw.description:
Dral has stopped keeping a column for the hole at Broadback and started keeping a page.

The salt crews who come back through the washes tell each other a story they don't tell outsiders. There's something in the standing water at the bottom that doesn't eat all year. It waits for the flood. When the cave fills, everything in it drowns at once, and the thing in the sump has its one meal and then waits another year.
fw_yearmaw.accept_text:
The flood is four months out, which means everything in the cave is alive, and the thing in the sump is as hungry as it ever gets.

The water never drains from the lowest bay, so go there. The thing in it has no eyes and has never needed any, and three of my drivers told me it waits until you move. It's in the Drowning Floor, at the foot of Broadback, west of the ramp, as far down as the cave goes. The crews call it Yearmaw.
fw_yearmaw.turn_in_text:
So the crews were right, and I've been filing their story under rumour for two years.

There's a page in my book for that too. I'm going to go and change it, and make a note of who told me first.
